liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Truckin'** (1 review): Hearing that forward playing in the Truckin' into The Other One stretch is a highlight for this reviewer [7]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Near the end of The Other One, Phil's bass becomes overwhelming, so heavy the reviewer imagines it wrecked an amp [16]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer calls this Morning Dew unique and lovely, the standout of the partial second set [9]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-10-21.set2-partial.sbd.miller.94409.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 6 songs; 78 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [1]. Said about its sound: Phil is far too loud in the mix while Keith and Billy are very low; Phil's bass is very loud and clear in the mix, giving a vivid picture of his playing; Uploader calls the mix horrible but better than having nothing [1][13][16]
- **gd1972-10-21.sbd.pset2.91505.flac16**: soundboard; 6 songs; 78 min; rated 3.9/5 by 10 [2]. Said about its sound: One player sits far forward in the mix, sometimes burying the rest of the band; Reviewer says the lead guitar tone resembles Zappa's; notes this recording is only a partial show; Reviewer describes the second-set excerpt as raw yet clean-sounding jamming [7][8][11][15]
- **gd1972-10-21.122342.sbd-pset2.rbbert.dan-fix.flac16**: soundboard; 6 songs; 72 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Goal was reducing bass prominence; most bass was in the right channel, sometimes both, so the left channel was reworked [3]
- **gd1972-10-21.set2-partial.sbd.rbbert.fix-94410.94453.flac16**: soundboard; 6 songs; 72 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [4]

## Around the show

- Full show also had a first set from Bertha to Playin' in the Band, Sugar Magnolia ending set two, and a Johnny B. Goode encore [10]
- Rain fell until showtime in Tennessee, then the day turned sunny and fall-like; reviewer, newly 18, attended [14]
- The Other One jamming matches the style heard on this song from late July through the end of 1972 [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-10-21.set2-partial.sbd.miller.94409.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> CD D [1]. Also: Possibly from a master cassette; uploader only fixed levels and cleaned up cuts; Tape flips occur during Greatest Story Ever Told and The Other One [1]
- **gd1972-10-21.sbd.pset2.91505.flac16**: transferred by JerryRocks; source: MSR>DAT>CDR>EAC>.WAV>TLH>.FLAC [2]
- **gd1972-10-21.122342.sbd-pset2.rbbert.dan-fix.flac16**: transferred by Dan McDonald; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> CD -> DC8; Reworked version of shnID 94453 [3]
- **gd1972-10-21.set2-partial.sbd.rbbert.fix-94410.94453.flac16**: transferred by rbbert; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> CD [4]. Also: This fix smoothed volume fluctuations in Truckin' and removed some dead air; Bass was lowered slightly in Truckin' starting about 3:44; Possibly from a master cassette, with tape flips in Greatest Story Ever Told and The Other One [4]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Vanderbilt University - October 21, 1972](https://www.dead.net/show/october-21-1972) [19]
- Poster by lostlivedead.blogspot.com: [October 21, 1972: Alumni Lawn, Vanderbilt University, Nashville, TN The Grateful Dead (Last Free Concert)](https://lostlivedead.blogspot.com/2013/04/october-21-1972-alumni-lawn-vanderbilt.html) [20]
